title: Tripping and sunny like the buck himself.
html_source:
While his name Malachi Mulligan reflects the dactylic hexameter of Homer, Buck describes his name and himself in the iambic pentameter of Shakespeare.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: “Tripping and sunny like the buck himself”, if you mean to suggest this self-description is an iambic pantameter—well it’s not: it’s a pentameter, sure, but it’s actually a fairly equal balance of trochaic (“Tripping”, “sunny”) and iambic (“the buck”, “himself”). Still, very good attention to detail for noting that this sentence does have 10 syllables; I didn’t realise.
